parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits sharply. The state/province tier is genuinely protective: public-accommodations and employment bans on gender identity, a hate-crime statute, open M/F/X documents, custody (including strip searches and housing) assigned by recognised gender identity, a care shield law, and a 'Most Protective' ranking with no facility ban. The national layer, however, imposes universal traveller-facing exposures that state law cannot displace: passport/visa sex-marker restrictions, an entry cable directing refusal on any sex discrepancy with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal single-sex facility exclusion, hostile federal custody practices (documented abuse in immigration detention, conversion-therapy policies in federal prisons), and foreign-government travel advisories. Severe custody harm is documented but attaches mainly to detained subsets; everyday exposure is administrative refusal, outing and facility friction. Protections are documented but rubric-based rather than enforcement-tested. Net: elevated-to-reduced risk, above screening-only anchors, below trained-border anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 end of X markers and non-birth-sex markers on national passports; Nov 2025 Supreme Court let restrictions take effect; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked abroad. Feb 2025 consular cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered. Eight governments issued travel advisories by Mar 2025.
entry_documents.protection: State issues M/F/X birth certificates, IDs and licences (resident-facing, climate signal only). Existing X passports valid until expiry. Litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ operates.
entry_documents.interaction: State openness cannot cure a federal visa refusal or passport restriction — the border desk is federal; discrepancy at entry can escalate into fraud proceedings.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 (hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution); transgender prisoner counts unpublished since 2025. In immigration custody, transgender men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Entry refusals have detaining neighbouring-country nationals.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State custody policy (since 1 July 2018) assigns housing, strip searches and clothing by recognised gender identity. Hate-crime statute covering gender identity; strengthened from 1 Oct 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor escalated from entry screening passes into the federal system, where the hostile custody policies apply and the state's protective custody rule does not.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Jan 2025 executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide — a universal exposure in federal buildings, courthouses and parks regardless of state law. Elsewhere 21+ states ban gender-congruent facility use; 4 criminalise it, one with a documented arrest (Mar 2025, trespass, 24h held in men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no facility ban in mapped categories and bans gender-identity discrimination in public places and government services; anti-bullying statute covers schools.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection governs state/private venues; federal facility exclusion operates inside the same state and cannot be waived locally.

care_services.exposure: Jan 2025 executive order calls youth gender-affirming care 'mutilation'; Oct 2025 proposed rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records in summer 2025; LGBTQ youth services removed from national crisis lifeline (Jul 2025). Several measures blocked or enjoined — status contested.
care_services.protection: 2022 shield law protects patients and providers from out-of-state civil or criminal charges — directly relevant to a visitor seeking lawful care here; conversion therapy on minors banned since May 2017.
care_services.interaction: Care sought here is shielded at state level, but federal record demands, funding rules and insurance policy reach the same encounter.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Dec 2025 DOJ cash-reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animi (not as a reward criterion); May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for prioritised identification and neutralisation while stating it will not target mere disagreement. Advocates compare the trajectory to early genocide stages. Officials cite 'mutilation' and direct criminal investigation of gender-affirming practice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime law covers gender identity/expression with additional penalties; employment discrimination prohibited nationally since 2020; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; gay-panic defence repealed in this state (2019).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises the temperature around any police encounter involving a documented discrepancy, while state charging and bias statutes work in the opposite direction.

minors_guardians.exposure: EO of 29 Jan 2025 directs law enforcement to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; EO of 28 Jan 2025 frames youth care as mutilation; Oct 2025 insurance rule targets under-18 care; hospital record subpoenas cover under-19s. Youth-care bans in 27 states.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law covers lawful youth care; state conversion-therapy ban; anti-bullying statute covers gender identity/expression on all school premises; 2021 ruling left trans girls' sports eligibility intact here.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family accessing care or school-type services here is protected locally, but federal investigative and record-subpoena powers remain operative.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific count of anti-trans violence or killings exists, so no comparison to the general homicide rate can be made. National bias statistics report sexual-orientation bias at one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias incidents. Foreign advisories warn trans travellers about identity-document and data rules. State-level data absent.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate crimes punishable nationally and under the state hate-crime statute (strengthened 1 Oct 2026); public-accommodations discrimination banned since 2011; documented arrest pattern in this state absent.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State bias statutes give a real complaint route the moment police respond; enforcement record for this state is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and multiple EO challenges unresolved; several orders enjoined, so operative rules shift by travel date. National risk assessment (13 Jul 2026) flagged 4 states 'Do Not Travel' for trans people and recorded continuing degradation; a Feb 2026 state law invalidating mismatched documents is called a template. Rubric-based 'Most Protective' ranking measures bills, not enforcement.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ on document rules, functioning state equality/hate-crime regime, courts have blocked several federal measures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty is concentrated at the federal layer; the state layer supplies predictable, documented remedies that federal pre-emption can override at borders and in federal facilities.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra runs a routine, universal exclusion register with appeals to the same agency. Here exclusion is contingent on document discrepancy, is litigated in independent courts, and the subnational layer actively protects public-accommodations access, custody placement and care. The analogue is the visa-refusal cable, not a standing bar.

Close to 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening, humiliating delays, refusal with slow and rarely revised appeals — closely matching this dossier's entry-document and visa-refusal exposure. This case is somewhat worse on custody severity (documented federal immigration abuse) but better on the state layer (documented protections that operate), producing a comparable net position.

Higher than 0.75-C: Meridia has trained border officers, respectful inspection, tribunal access and low detention severity. Here the national posture is explicitly restrictive — markers eliminated, discrepancy-refusal cable, facility exclusion, custody conversion policies and external travel advisories — which is a heavier documented exposure than Meridia's residual discretion.

parsed.synthesis: Two sovereign layers operate at once. The state/province supplies documented, comparatively strong machinery — non-discrimination in public places and services, hate-crime coverage, gender-identity custody placement including strip searches, a care shield law, open M/F/X documents, a conversion-therapy ban — and sits in a 'Most Protective' tier with no facility ban. The national regime supplies the exposures a visitor actually meets first: eliminated passport markers, a consular cable ordering refusal on any sex discrepancy with possible lifetime fraud finding, federal single-sex facility exclusion, hostile federal custody (conversion-therapy corrections policy; documented abuse in immigration detention), record subpoenas and adversarial official framing. State protections cannot displace border, federal-facility or federal-custody authority. Severity is administrative-to-major in ordinary travel (refusal, outing, facility friction, stranding) but rises to severe in the lower-probability custody path. Enforcement of the state's protections is rubric-documented, not incident-tested, and national rules are in active litigation, so outcomes vary by moment of travel.
